odia: ହାଣ୍ଡିରେ ଖାଏ, ଗୋଡ଼ରେ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ଗାଧୋଇ ଯାଏ
title: Good enough to eat, too much to touch
literal_meaning: One eats from the pot, but goes to bathe when its contents fall on the foot.
explanation: The same food is welcome in the mouth and suddenly objectionable on the foot. That abrupt change is the comic hinge of the line: acceptance in one situation turns into an elaborate response in another. The dictionary supplies the bathing sense but no separate moral gloss. Our reading treats the contrast as a possible tease about selective fastidiousness or inconsistent standards. It does not establish that bathing is always excessive, or that a particular ritual or community is being described.
meaning_odia: ହାଣ୍ଡିରୁ ଖାଇବା ବେଳେ ଯାହା ଗ୍ରହଣୀୟ, ସେହି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଗୋଡ଼ରେ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ଗାଧୋଇବାକୁ ଯିବାର କଥା ଆସୁଛି। ଏକେ ଜିନିଷକୁ ଦୁଇ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିରେ ଏତେ ଅଲଗା ଭାବେ ନେବାରେ ଏହାର ହାସ୍ୟ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଗାଧୋଇବା କ୍ରିୟାର ଉଦାହରଣ ଭାବେ କଥାଟି ଅଛି; ଅଲଗା ନୀତିକଥା ଦିଆଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଏହି ବିପରୀତ ଆଚରଣକୁ ଧରି ଅତି ବାଛବିଚାର ବା ବଦଳୁଥିବା ମାପକାଠିକୁ ଥଟ୍ଟା କରିହୁଏ। ସ୍ୱରଟି ଘନିଷ୍ଠ ହସର ହୋଇପାରେ, ପୁଣି ତାଚ୍ଛଲ୍ୟର ମଧ୍ୟ ହୋଇପାରେ।
english_summary: The contrast invites a teasing question about standards that change with the situation.
odia_summary: ଏକେ ଜିନିଷ ପାଇଁ ଦୁଇ ମାପକାଠି ରଖିବାକୁ ଖୋଚା ଦେଉଥିବା ଚିତ୍ର।
usage_example: Original imagined example: A friend happily eats a sticky sweet with their fingers, then protests loudly when a little syrup touches their shoe. Another friend quotes the saying with a smile while offering a cloth. This harmless transfer is editorial, not a documented historical use.
cultural_context: No named caste, purity rule or bathing custom is inferred. The interpretation of inconsistent standards is editorial close reading; the source attests the words and literal verb.
